channel.description: math.GR updates on the arXiv.org e-print archive.

item.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
item.description: arXiv:2611.28382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\in\gamma_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for a word with six syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Keren

item.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leq\Gamma_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Dang, Jianchun Wu

item.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du

item.title: Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Khukhro, Pavel Shumyatsky

item.title: Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Steinmann

item.title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.
item.dc:creator: Kun Zhang, Yuanyang Zhou

item.title: On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $\sigma$-permutable subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\sigma=\{\sigma_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $\sigma$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $\sigma$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.
item.dc:creator: Chenxiao Lin

item.title: Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $\alpha$ can be chosen with $[P,\alpha,\alpha]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $\alpha$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,\alpha,\alpha,\alpha]=1$, and with $[P,\alpha,\alpha]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.
item.dc:creator: M. Yasir K{\i}zmaz

item.title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
item.description: arXiv:2611.29587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Popoff

item.title: Products of supersoluble groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.
item.dc:creator: Jinbao Li, Yong Yang

item.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.29667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.
item.dc:creator: John W. MacQuarrie, Peter Symonds

item.title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
item.description: arXiv:2611.29812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G = *_\lambda G_\lambda$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Strietelmeier

item.title: Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based
item.description: arXiv:2611.30129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.
item.dc:creator: Haihong Wu

item.title: Groups with dual classes of subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely characterize insoluble groups whose subgroups are pronormal or pronormalize every subgroup. We also completely describe $p$-groups with this property, and prove many structural results in the soluble case (for example, such groups are always of length at most $3$ and have Sylow towers).
item.dc:creator: E. Ingrosso, M. Trombetti, A. Zitouni

item.title: Asymptotic insolubility of alternating groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $a,b\in\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)$ with $a\neq 1$, and let $s$ be chosen uniformly in $A_n$. We show that the probability that $\langle a, bs\rangle$ is insoluble tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly in $a$ and $b$. More precisely, this probability is at least $1-O(n^{-1/24})$. The proof combines a bound in terms of the support of $a$ with estimates on permutations lying in transitive subgroups of the symmetric group.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Lucchini

item.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
item.description: arXiv:2611.30569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Beltr\'an, Changguo Shao

item.title: Hyperbolicity and zero divisors in random graphical groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a criterion for hyperbolicity of random groups presented by labelled graphs. On $n$ vertices, we prescribe the proportions of the possible sets of outgoing labels. For each generator, we choose a uniform matching between its occurrences and those of its inverse, independently across generators. We condition the graph to have girth at least $\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$ for sufficiently small $c>0$, and take the labels of closed paths as relators. The distribution of outgoing labels determines a matrix of turn weights. Suppose that each letter occurs as often as its inverse and with positive frequency, every vertex has degree at least three, and the entrywise square of the turn matrix has spectral radius less than one. We prove that, with probability tending to one as $n$ grows, the resulting group is torsion-free and non-elementary hyperbolic and admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space. On the same event, every path from a prescribed root to a different vertex has nontrivial label in the group. The proof uses the spectral radius bound to control repeated path labels in diagrams and a local-to-global argument to obtain a linear isoperimetric inequality. Applied to OpenAI's characteristic-two zero-divisor construction, the criterion recovers the hyperbolicity result of Mghirbi and Douglas.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Winston Lee, Alexei Miasnikov, Kyrylo Muliarchyk

item.title: Strong Banach property $(T)$ for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.30842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.
item.dc:creator: Jvbin Yao

item.title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on

item.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
item.description: arXiv:2611.28494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/\Gamma$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $\Gamma$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to M\"obius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.29073v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.
item.dc:creator: Satyanath Howladar, Lorenzo Ruffoni

item.title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the larger sum from degree four on.
item.dc:creator: Manoj Kumar Singh

item.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.
item.dc:creator: Huynh Viet Khanh

item.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.30856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $\sigma$-local compactness, $\sigma$-compactness, the Lindel\"of property, and left $\omega$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindel\"of property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.
item.dc:creator: Tayomara Borsich, Pedro J. Chocano

item.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.30871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo

item.title: Metric structure in Hecke-induced modules for groups acting on buildings
item.description: arXiv:2611.30901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a thick locally finite building of type $(W, S)$ and $G$ be a locally compact group acting properly and chamber-transitively on $X$. We give a condition on a Hermitian module $(V_0, \varphi_0)$ of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra $\mathbf C_{\mathbf q}[W]$ ensuring that the natural $G$-invariant form defined on the induced $G$-module has the same negative index as $\varphi_0$, where ${\mathbf q}$ is the thickness vector of $X$. It implies that induction of Hecke-modules preserves unitarity. In the affine case, this recovers results by Matsumoto, Barbasch--Moy and Ciubotaru. In general, assuming that $G$ is Weyl-transitive, we obtain new irreducible $G$-representations on Hilbert spaces as well as on infinite-dimensional symmetric spaces of finite rank. Using Hecke-modules of Lorentzian signature, we also derive new obstructions to Kazhdan's property (T), showing that the known sufficient conditions in terms of the thickness are mostly necessary.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Emmanuel Caprace, Alex Lou\'e, Andreas Thom

item.title: Codimension two complements in hyperbolic products
item.description: arXiv:2611.30926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-volume locally symmetric manifold modeled on $\H^m \times \H^n$, and let $S$ be a compact, totally geodesic, codimension two submanifold of $M$ modeled on $\H^{m-1} \times \H^{n-1}$. In this paper, we initiate the study of manifolds of the form $N = M \setminus S$. In the case where $M$ is a product and $S$ is connected, we prove that such $N$ admit complete, finite-volume, $A$-regular metrics with non-positive sectional curvature. We also deduce some topological properties of $N$, and algebraic properties of $\pi_1(N)$. In the case where $M$ is irreducible, we show that $N$ admits {\it almost non-positive curvature}. Similar results hold for manifolds $X_d$, which are $d$-fold branched covers of $M$ ramified over $S$. Along the way, we show that there are infinitely many commensurability classes of such pairs $(M,S)$, and develop general curvature formulas for doubly warped product metrics, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Hyeran Cho, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lafont, Nicholas Miller, Barry Minemyer

item.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
item.description: arXiv:2203.12250v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.
item.dc:creator: Doron Puder, Tomer Zimhoni

item.title: Primitivity Testing in Free Group Algebras via Duality
item.description: arXiv:2502.12885v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a free group. By a classical result of Cohn and Lewin, the free group algebra $K\left[F\right]$ is a free ideal ring (FIR): a ring over which the submodules of free modules are themselves free, and of a well-defined rank. Given a finitely generated right ideal $I\leq K\left[F\right]$ and an element $f\in I$, we give an explicit algorithm determining whether $f$ is part of some basis of $I$. More generally, given free $K[F]$-modules $M\le N$, we provide algorithms determining whether $M$ is a free summand of $N$, and whether $N$ admits a free splitting relative to $M$. These can also be used to obtain analogous algorithms for free groups $H\le J$. As an aside, we also provide an algorithm to compute the intersection of two given submodules of a free $K\left[F\right]$-module. A key feature of this work is the introduction of a duality, induced by a matrix with entries in a free ideal ring, between the respective algebraic extensions of its column and row spaces.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), no. 6, e70599
item.dc:creator: Matan Seidel, Danielle Ernst-West, Doron Puder

item.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
item.description: arXiv:2604.02087v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a strict partial order $\Delta$ on a set $\Lambda$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(\Delta)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(\Delta)$, where $\Delta$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(\Delta)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$\Delta$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(\Delta)/G(\Gamma)\cong G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$, where $\Gamma$ is a normal subset of $\Delta$, and $G(\Gamma)$ and $G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.
item.dc:creator: Leandro Cagliero, Fernando Szechtman

item.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2604.09014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
item.description: arXiv:2606.11461v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.
item.dc:creator: Agust\'in D'Alessandro, Fernando Szechtman

item.title: The number of composite class sizes in finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.27977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider finite groups with at least three conjugacy class sizes that are composite numbers and we prove that, in that situation, the number of prime class sizes is bounded by the number of composite class sizes. The analogous result for (non-)prime-power class sizes is also addressed.
item.dc:creator: Vittorio Bagnara, V\'ictor Sotomayor

item.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
item.description: arXiv:2607.11161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $\phi$ and $\psi$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\psi$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^\phi$ and $G_x^\psi$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $\phi$ and $\psi$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $\phi$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.
item.dc:creator: Nepur Ranjan Hazarika, Kukil Kalpa Rajkhowa

item.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.21817v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Primoz Moravec

item.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
item.description: arXiv:2608.27593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.
item.dc:creator: Noam Ta Shma

item.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.21255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.
item.dc:creator: Izhar Oppenheim

item.title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.15156v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.
item.dc:creator: Jingjing Duan, Lijian An

item.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
item.description: arXiv:2611.21875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $\beta_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leq\beta=\beta_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $\beta\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Hillman

item.title: Character codegrees in $\pi$-separable groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.23799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_{\pi}(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $\pi$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(\chi)=|G:\ker\chi|/\chi(1)$) are $\pi$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $\pi$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_{\pi}(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}$-characters $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Jiakuan Lu, Wei Meng, Liping Xie

item.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
item.description: arXiv:2611.24745v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a crystallographic root system $\Phi$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}\Phi$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $\rho + \lambda$, where $\rho$ is the Weyl vector and $\lambda$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $\rho$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dutour Sikiri\'c

item.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2409.16571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].
item.dc:creator: Danielle Ernst-West, Doron Puder, Yotam Shomroni

item.title: Amenability of group actions on compact spaces and the associated Banach algebras
item.description: arXiv:2504.08357v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a topological group $G$, amenability can be characterized by the amenability of the convolution Banach algebra $L^1(G)$. Here a Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every bounded derivation from $A$ into any dual--type $A$--$A$--Banach bimodule is inner. We extend this classical result to the case of discrete group actions on compact Hausdorff spaces in our main theorem Theorem 5.2. By using a Banach algebra naturally associated with the action and adopting a suitably weakened notion of amenability for Banach algebras, we obtain an analogous characterization of amenable actions. As a lemma, we also proved a fixed--point property for amenable actions in Theorem 4.4 that strengthens the theorem of Dong and Wang (2015).
item.dc:creator: Hikaru Awazu

item.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.08988v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.
item.dc:creator: Michael Magee, Doron Puder, Ramon van Handel

item.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15419v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.
item.dc:creator: F. V. Weinstein

item.title: Separately continuous maps into regular spaces and continuity of operations in separable semitopological groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.04891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every regular separable feebly compact semitopological group is a topological group. This answers a question of M. Tkachenko (2014) and extends the separable case of the author's 1994 theorem on Tychonoff pseudocompact groups to regular spaces. The proof rests on a new result: if $X$ is a separable Baire space, $Y$ is feebly compact and $Z$ is regular, then every separately continuous map $X\times Y\to Z$ is strongly quasicontinuous. Previously this was known only when $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are Tychonoff. Using topological games of Banach-Mazur type, we extend the group theorem to regular separable Baire groups from a wider class of spaces, which contains all $p$-spaces, all feebly compact spaces and all products of a $p$-space with a feebly compact space. We also obtain local versions: the theorem holds for locally separable, locally feebly compact groups.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Reznichenko

item.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
item.description: arXiv:2611.13459v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.
item.dc:creator: Eilidh McKemmie
